item.title: Aviation Safety Claims Belong in NTSB and FAA Primary Records
item.description: How to evaluate manufacturing, maintenance, and accident narratives using NTSB investigations and FAA public portals — not viral corporate conspiracy frames.

item.title: Election Security and AI Risk Frameworks: What Primary Institutions Actually Publish
item.description: CISA election-security guidance and NIST’s AI Risk Management Framework define the public baseline for infrastructure protection and model risk — without requiring unverified incident claims.

item.title: Judicial Ethics Starts With the Court’s Own Code — Not Viral Gift Lists Alone
item.description: The Supreme Court’s November 13, 2023 Code of Conduct for Justices is the primary institutional text for ethics claims about the Court; secondary reporting must still attach to primary documents.

item.title: Debt Transparency Without the Panic: FiscalData, Monthly Treasury Statements, and Fed Rate Tables
item.description: How to read the federal debt position from primary Treasury datasets and Federal Reserve statistical releases — and what those sources do not claim.

item.title: AIPAC Has Spent $28 Million Reshaping Congress in 2026. Here Is Where the Money Went.
item.description: The most powerful foreign policy lobby in America is funneling record sums through shell super PACs to defeat candidates who support conditioning U.S. aid to Israel. The Illinois primaries reveal the full playbook.

item.title: Boeing's Culture of Silence: Inside the Whistleblower Deaths and the FAA's Failure to Protect Safety
item.description: The unexplained death of quality control engineer John Barnett, following threats from Boeing management, exposes systemic failures in aircraft safety oversight and regulatory capture of the Federal Aviation Administration.

item.title: The DOJ Has Released 3.5 Million Pages of Epstein Files. Here Is What They Contain.
item.description: The largest disclosure of criminal case materials in American history includes 2,000 videos, 180,000 images, and records from five federal investigations — and has exposed catastrophic failures in victim privacy protections.

item.title: The Federal Reserve Holds Rates Steady as Iran Conflict Roils Global Oil Markets
item.description: With the federal funds rate anchored at 3.5–3.75% and crude oil prices surging past $110 per barrel, the central bank faces its most consequential policy crossroads since 2008.

item.title: Gaza Faces UN-Declared Famine Amid Aid Blockade: The Humanitarian Catastrophe Beyond the Headlines
item.description: The United Nations formally declared Gaza in famine conditions on March 15, 2026, marking the first UN famine declaration since 2011 as international institutions struggle to force open humanitarian corridors.

item.title: Congress Races to Reform FISA Section 702 Before April Sunset. Here Is What the Bill Would Change.
item.description: The bipartisan Government Surveillance Reform Act would require warrants for FBI searches, close the data broker loophole, and restore oversight of the secret FISA court — the most significant surveillance reform since the Snowden disclosures.

item.title: The $36 Trillion Debt: How Interest Payments Became America's Largest Budget Item
item.description: As the national debt surpasses $36 trillion, the federal government spends more on interest payments than on defense, education, or healthcare—a milestone that redefines fiscal policy constraints.

item.title: The 145% Tariff Wall: Trump's Trade War With China Redefines Supply Chains and Consumer Prices
item.description: As the Trump administration imposes unprecedented tariffs on Chinese goods, American consumers face surging inflation while supply chains built over three decades come under stress.

item.title: $1.5 Trillion: The Pentagon’s Proposed 2027 Budget Would Be the Largest in American History
item.description: Coming on the heels of an $839 billion FY2026 appropriation and a $152 billion reconciliation boost, the White House is requesting a defense budget that exceeds the GDP of all but 12 nations on Earth.

item.title: A Note on Methodology, Evidence Standards & How to Read This Book
item.description: This is a reference work. It compiles primary source documents — court records, congressional testimony, declassified government files, academic studies, and verified financial disclosures — into a single chronological narrative.
